column1: # The wire's own bytes, for anyone implementing a receiver or a server
# (`INPUT.md` section 15, DEC-1759 lesson 3). The engine and the server run
# every row; the engine keeps an exact copy of this file, which its commit
# gate compares, as `neoteletext_web::wire_vectors::TABLE`, and the server
# reads that copy, as both read the address map's table.
# Four columns, separated by tabs: kind, name, value, meaning.
# version  value is what both sides must say; meaning says where.
# close    value is a close code; meaning is what a receiver does.
# input    value is one message of the input stream, in hexadecimal; meaning
#          is the item it reads as. It writes back to the same bytes unless
#          the name begins `skipped`, and a server told it does as meaning says.
# refused  value is a message a reader must refuse: a protocol error, closed
# record   value is one 42-byte packet 4/31 on data channel 12, service 0,
#          record id as meaning says, in hexadecimal; meaning is the record.
